items.toString: build-node-image - ENOSPC disk exhaustion on ppc64le build workers (2 builds affected)

h2. Build Details
||Build||Stream||Arch||Jenkins URL||
|[#6889|https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-node-image/6889/]|4.22\-9.8|ppc64le|[link|https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-node-image/6889/]|
|[#6890|https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-node-image/6890/]|4.22\-10.2|ppc64le|[link|https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-node-image/6890/]|

h2. Root Cause Analysis
* *Classification*: infrastructure
* *Confidence*: high

Both builds failed due to disk exhaustion \(ENOSPC\) on the Jenkins worker nodes during ppc64le operations. In both cases, x86\_64, aarch64, and s390x completed successfully — ppc64le was the last architecture processed and hit disk full.

* *#6889 \(4.22\-9.8\):* Disk exhausted while decompressing the ppc64le qcow2 image for kola testing. All 4 arch node\-image containers had already been built and pushed; x86\_64/aarch64/s390x qcow2s had already been decompressed. ppc64le was last and failed mid\-stream.
* *#6890 \(4.22\-10.2\):* Disk exhausted immediately on ppc64le podman build launch \(mkdir /var/tmp/libpod\_builder16973238 failed within 1 second\). x86\_64, aarch64, s390x all built and pushed successfully.

Both builds were transient — subsequent builds for their respective streams succeeded \(#6897 for 4.22\-9.8, #6904 for 4.22\-10.2\).

h2. Evidence
h3. Log Excerpt — #6889 \(4.22\-9.8\)
{code}
gzip: stdout: No space left on device
Failed in branch ppc64le
{code}

h3. Log Excerpt — #6890 \(4.22\-10.2\)
{code}
Error: mkdir /var/tmp/libpod_builder16973238: no space left on device
Failed in branch ppc64le
{code}

h3. Patterns Observed
* ENOSPC failure isolated to ppc64le in both builds \(last arch processed in parallel pipeline\)
* Disk exhaustion accumulates across arches; ppc64le consistently the arch to tip over
* prune\-container\-resources.service does not clean dangling node\-staging images, contributing to disk buildup

h2. Upstream Links
* *Related Issues*: [https://github.com/coreos/fedora\-coreos\-pipeline/issues/1365|https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-pipeline/issues/1365] — prune\-container\-resources.service does not clean dangling node\-staging images \(OPEN\)

h2. Resolution
* *Status*: resolved \(transient — streams self\-healed\)
* *Retry Build \(4.22\-9.8\)*: #6897 \(succeeded\)
* *Retry Build \(4.22\-10.2\)*: #6904 \(succeeded\)
* *Recommended action*: Add podman prune / workspace cleanup step to build\-node\-image pipeline to prevent recurrence. Track upstream fix in fedora\-coreos\-pipeline#1365. Monitor for further ENOSPC failures on ppc64le workers.

items.toString: This work item relates to COS-4560

h2. Root Cause
The Kubernetes worker pod's {{worker}} container was OOMKilled \(exit code 137 / SIGKILL\) during kola testing. The pod has a 10752Mi memory limit but kola runs with {{\-\-parallel=5}}, scheduling multiple memory\-intensive tests concurrently \(ISO install tests requiring \~4096 MiB each, FIPS tests, LUKS reprovision tests\). Kola's memory scheduler logged repeated "Waiting on memory" warnings with available RAM dropping as low as 268 MiB. All tests that completed before the crash were PASSING — this is a pure infrastructure failure.

h2. Affected Builds
||Build||Stream||Arch||Jenkins URL||
|build\-arch #5326|rhel\-9.6|s390x|[#5326|https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-arch/5326/]|
|build #5220|c9s|x86\_64|[#5220|https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build/5220/]|

{quote}
*Note:* build\-arch #5326 metadata labels s390x but console log content references c9s/x86\_64 — possible label mismatch, investigate on retry.

{quote}

h2. Root Cause Analysis
* *Classification*: infrastructure
* *Confidence*: high

Kola's parallel test execution exhausts the 10752Mi memory limit of the worker container. With {{\-\-parallel=5}} and ISO install tests each requiring \~4096 MiB of RAM, the aggregate memory demand far exceeds the pod limit. The OOM killer terminates the {{worker}} container \(exit 137\), aborting the entire test run regardless of per\-test results.

h2. Evidence
h3. Key Log Line
{code}
worker -- terminated (137)
{code}

h3. Patterns Observed
* Kola repeatedly logged "Waiting on memory" prior to OOMKill
* Available memory reached as low as 268 MiB during test scheduling
* All tests that completed before the crash returned PASS — failure is not test\-related
* Exit code 137 = SIGKILL from kernel OOM killer

h2. History / Prior Occurrences
This is a *recurring known issue*. Prior COS tickets tracked the same root cause and were never given a systemic fix:
\- COS\-4460, COS\-4546, COS\-4559, COS\-4560 \(across rhel\-9.8, c10s, rhel\-10.2 streams\)
\- COS\-4649 \(most recent prior occurrence — also tracked build #5220 before it was closed\)

h2. Resolution
* *Status*: unresolved \(systemic fix pending\)
* *Immediate action*: Rerun both builds — transient, likely to pass on retry
* *Systemic fix options* \(either or both\):
## Increase worker container memory limit beyond 10752Mi
## Reduce kola {{\-\-parallel}} from 5 to 3 or 4 to cap peak concurrent memory demand

## Build Details

|| Build || Stream || Arch || Jenkins URL ||
| #5216 | 4.14-9.2 | x86_64 | https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build/5216/ |
| #5209 | 4.14-9.2 | x86_64 | https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build/5209/ |

## Root Cause Analysis
- *Classification*: flake
- *Confidence*: high

Two builds with independent sets of transient failures, all self-healed on rerun.

h3. Build #5216 — quay.io unexpected EOF
Failed during extensions-container build with {{unexpected EOF}} pulling {{quay.io/fedora/fedora:38}} from the quay.io CDN — a transient network glitch. {{podman build}} has no retry logic for this error, so the build failed immediately.

h3. Build #5209 — three kola test flakes
Three independent kola test flakes (all with {{rerun_failed: false}}):

# *ostree.hotfix/persist* — GitHub {{raw.githubusercontent.com}} returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited) when downloading the {{aht-dummy}} RPM during the test.
# *ext.config.shared.kdump.crash* — {{kdump.service}} stuck in {{activating}} state for the full 60-second timeout; kdump failed to load.
# *ext.config.shared.ignition.remote* — VM entered {{emergency.target}} in initramfs — transient provisioning issue.

*Note*: The pipeline exits FAILURE because {{--allow-rerun-success}} only covers {{tags=needs-internet}} tests, and {{kdump.crash}} does not carry that tag, so its flake is not automatically forgiven.

## Evidence

h3. Build #5216 — Log Excerpt
{code}
Error: reading blob from source image: reading blob sha256:...: unexpected EOF
podman build: exit status 1
{code}

h3. Build #5209 — Log Excerpt
{code}
# ostree.hotfix/persist
Error: GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../aht-dummy-*.rpm: 429 Too Many Requests

# ext.config.shared.kdump.crash
kdump.service: start operation timed out. Terminating.
Failed to start Crash recovery kernel arming.

# ext.config.shared.ignition.remote
[  TIME  ] Timed out waiting for device...
Welcome to emergency mode!
{code}

h3. Patterns Observed
- All failures are transient (passed on rerun): classic flake behaviour
- Build #5216: quay.io CDN network glitch — no retry in podman build
- Build #5209: GitHub rate-limiting for raw asset download during kola test
- Build #5209: kdump activation timeout — intermittent service startup
- Build #5209: initramfs emergency.target — transient VM provisioning
- {{--allow-rerun-success}} scope does not cover {{kdump.crash}}, causing a pipeline FAILURE despite the flake

## Upstream Links
- *Test Source (kdump)*: https://github.com/coreos/coreos-assembler/tree/main/mantle/kola/tests

## Resolution
- *Status*: resolved (self-healed on rerun)
- *Recommended actions*:
## No immediate action needed — both failures are self-healing.
## Consider mirroring the {{aht-dummy}} RPM internally to avoid GitHub rate-limits for {{ostree.hotfix/persist}}.
## Consider widening {{--allow-rerun-success}} scope beyond {{tags=needs-internet}} to cover {{kdump.crash}} flakes.
## Monitor {{kdump.crash}} flake frequency; if it increases, investigate kdump service startup reliability.

## Build Details
- *Job*: build-arch
- *Build*: #5318
- *Stream*: 4.18-9.4
- *Architecture*: ppc64le
- *Duration*: 129 min (estimated 74 min, 1.7× overrun)
- *Jenkins URL*: https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-arch/5318/

## Root Cause Analysis
- *Classification*: infrastructure
- *Confidence*: high

The ppc64le Jenkins worker ran out of disk space during {{cosa compress}} (gzip of {{metal.ppc64le.raw}}). Three contributing factors combined to exhaust available disk:

# Concurrent build overlap: {{build-arch}} #5315 (stream {{rhel-10.2}}, ppc64le) overlapped by ~19 minutes, leaving residual artifacts on the shared worker before workspace cleanup completed.
# Testiso timeout flakes: Three {{miniso-install}} kola tests ({{miniso-install.ppcfw}}, {{miniso-install.nm.ppcfw}}, {{miniso-install.4k.ppcfw}}) timed out and accumulated temporary qemu VM artifacts — adding ~30 min of extra runtime and disk usage.
# Extended build duration: Build ran 1.7× longer than estimated (129 min vs 74 min), increasing the window for disk pressure.

*Prior occurrence*: COS-4529 (closed) — same class of failure on ppc64le worker.

## Evidence

h3. Log Excerpt
{code}
gzip: stdout: No space left on device
subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['gzip', '-6', '-c',
  'builds/418.94.202607091625-0/ppc64le/rhcos-418.94.202607091625-0-metal.ppc64le.raw']'
  returned non-zero exit status 1.
failed to execute cmd-compress: exit status 1
{code}

h3. Patterns Observed
- ENOSPC on shared ppc64le Jenkins worker during artifact compression
- Concurrent build (#5315, rhel-10.2) ran simultaneously on the same worker
- Three testiso flakes added ~30 min runtime and temp qemu artifacts
- Build runtime 1.7× over estimate — extended disk pressure window

## Upstream Links
- *Related Issues*: COS-4529 (closed — prior ENOSPC occurrence on ppc64le)

## Resolution
- *Status*: retry-pending
- *Recommended actions*:
## Rerun the build — transient; a clean worker should succeed.
## Investigate workspace cleanup between concurrent ppc64le builds to prevent artifact accumulation.
## Consider adding disk capacity or stricter concurrency limits for ppc64le workers to prevent recurrence.

Both failures are transient server-side/network issues with {{registry.ci.openshift.org}}, unrelated to build content. Both streams self-healed on subsequent runs.

*Build #6804 (4.22-9.8, 2026-07-08):* registry.ci.openshift.org returned HTTP 500 during blob upload while {{podman push --retry 5}} was uploading the aarch64 extensions container image. All other arch builds and pushes succeeded. Only the aarch64 extensions push was affected. Failed after exhausting all 5 retries (628s total).

*Build #6770 (4.19-9.6, 2026-07-07):* DNS resolution failure ({{Temporary failure in name resolution}}) when {{skopeo inspect}} attempted to contact {{registry.ci.openshift.org}} for x86_64 and aarch64 arches. s390x and ppc64le succeeded.

h2. Evidence

h3. Log Excerpt - Build #6804

{noformat}received unexpected HTTP status: 500
podman push --retry 5 registry.ci.openshift.org/.../node-image-4.22-9.8:aarch64-extensions{noformat}

h3. Log Excerpt - Build #6770

{noformat}Temporary failure in name resolution
skopeo inspect docker://registry.ci.openshift.org/...{noformat}

h3. Patterns Observed

* Both failures are server-side errors from registry.ci.openshift.org (HTTP 500 and DNS resolution failure)
* Failures are transient: subsequent runs succeeded without any code changes
* Partial-arch impact: only certain architectures affected per build, consistent with transient network/infra conditions
* Fast failure pattern: Build #6804 completed in ~628s after exhausting podman push retries

h2. Resolution

* *Status*: Resolved (self-healed)
* Both streams recovered on subsequent runs with no code changes required
* *Recommended action*: If {{registry.ci.openshift.org}} failures cluster further, escalate to the CI registry team (DPTP/TestPlatform)

h2. Build Details

* Job: build-node-image
* Builds: #6831, #6785
* Streams: 5.0-9.8, 4.19-9.6
* Timestamps: #6831 — 2026-07-08T15:26Z | #6785 — 2026-07-07T22:00Z
* Jenkins URL #6831: https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-node-image/6831/
* Jenkins URL #6785: https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-node-image/6785/

h2. Root Cause Analysis

* Classification: infra-flake (known upstream podman/buildah bug)
* Confidence: high

podman build returns exit status 125 with 'error deleting build container: identifier is not a container' after the image is successfully built and tagged. This occurs during post-build cleanup when concurrent parallel arch builds share overlayfs layers/container storage. The actual image build and tagging succeeds in all cases — only the automatic container cleanup step fails.

This is a recurrence of a known pattern (see also: COS-4586 for build #6613, 4.23-9.8 — same root cause, closed).

h2. Affected Builds

||Build||Stream||Arch(es) Failed||Arch(es) OK||Timestamp||
|#6831|5.0-9.8|x86_64|aarch64, ppc64le, s390x|2026-07-08T15:26Z|
|#6785|4.19-9.6|s390x, ppc64le, x86_64|aarch64|2026-07-07T22:00Z|

h2. Evidence

h3. Log Excerpt

{noformat}error deleting build container: identifier is not a container
exit status 125{noformat}

h3. Patterns Observed

* podman build exits 125 on cleanup despite image being successfully built and tagged
* Failure isolated to post-build container removal step (not the image build itself)
* Container ID already tagged/committed before the cleanup error fires
* Multiple arches fail per build, consistent with parallel build contention on shared overlayfs/container storage
* Streams self-healed on subsequent reruns (#6841 for 5.0-9.8, #6793 for 4.19-9.6)

h2. Upstream Links

* Related Issues: https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/11775 (upstream podman race in build container cleanup)
* Prior COS tracking: COS-4586 (build #6613, 4.23-9.8, same root cause — closed)

h2. Resolution

* Status: self-healed (resolved via rerun)
* Retry Builds: #6841 (5.0-9.8), #6793 (4.19-9.6)
* Recommended Mitigation: Serialize extensions podman build calls per-arch, or pass --rm=false to skip automatic build-container cleanup and handle removal explicitly. Addresses recurring flake without requiring upstream fix.

## Build Details
- **Job**: build
- **Build**: #5202
- **Stream**: 4.14-9.2
- **Architecture**: x86_64
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-08T19:52Z
- **Version**: 414.92.202607081956-0
- **Jenkins URL**: https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build/5202/

## Root Cause Analysis
- **Classification**: infra-flake
- **Confidence**: high

The `iso-install.bios` kola testiso test timed out after exactly 10m0s with no diagnostic output. All 17 other testiso tests passed, including `iso-offline-install.bios`, `miniso-install.bios`, and `pxe-online-install.bios`. This is consistent with a transient QEMU VM hang or I/O stall rather than a systematic boot regression. `kola testiso` does not support `--rerun`, so no automatic retry was attempted.

A secondary `ostree.hotfix/install` failure (GitHub HTTP 429 rate limit) was also present but passed on rerun — confirmed flake, not the root cause.

## Evidence

### Log Excerpt
```
--- FAIL: iso-install.bios (10m0.000s)
        timeout: test timed out after 10m0s
```

### Patterns Observed
- Exact 10m0s timeout indicates the test hit the deadline with no progress — characteristic of a QEMU VM hang or transient I/O stall
- All 17 other testiso tests passed in the same build run
- Secondary HTTP 429 rate-limit flake confirmed unrelated (passed on rerun)

### Package Changes vs Last Good Build (#5133)
| Package | Previous | Current |
|---------|----------|---------|
| kernel | 5.14.0-284.179.1.el9_2 | 5.14.0-284.180.1.el9_2 |
| nftables | 1.0.4-11.el9_2.2 | 1.0.4-11.el9_2.3 |

## Upstream Links
- **Package Build**: kernel-5.14.0-284.180.1.el9_2 (potential regression candidate if timeout recurs)
- **Test Source**: https://github.com/coreos/coreos-assembler/blob/main/tests/kola/testiso

## Resolution
- **Status**: retry-pending
- **Recommended Action**: Rerun with STREAM=4.14-9.2 FORCE=true. If the timeout recurs, download kola-testiso artifacts and inspect VM console output to determine whether kernel-5.14.0-284.180.1.el9_2 introduces a BIOS boot regression.

[4817188518] Upstream Reporter: Joel Capitao
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}Related to https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-tracker/issues/2173
We need to enable the verification of the RPM signature in Konflux (currently disabled).
Below the steps:

1. Create one policy for each type of streams: `development` and `production`
2. Enable the RPM signature verification in the `production` policy
3. Keep disable for `development` one

When fast-tracking/pinning RPMs, most of the time those do not have a signed _version_ yet in some repo. But as soon as our `bump-lockfile` job promote them, they are tagged in `coreos-pool` and then signed. So the PR testing the fast-tracking cannot expect them to be signed. That's why we need to disable signature checking only for `development` streams.
{quote}

Upstream description: {quote}Related to https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-tracker/issues/2173
We need to enable the verification of the RPM signature in Konflux (currently disabled).
Below the steps:

1. Create one policy for each type of streams: `development` and `production`
2. Enable the RPM signature verification in the `production` policy
3. Keep disable for `development` one

When fast-tracking/pinning RPMs, most of the time those do not have a signed _version_ yet in some repo. But as soon as our `bump-lockfile` job promote them, they are tagged in `coreos-pool` and then signed. So the PR testing the fast-tracking cannot expect them to be signed. That's why we need to disable signature checking only for `development` streams.
{quote}

h2. Root Cause Analysis
* *Classification*: flake \(test\_regression\)
* *Confidence*: High

The kola test {{ext.config.shared.selinux.file\-context\-policy\-match}} intermittently fails when executed in the non\-exclusive test bucket concurrently with another test that invokes podman. The podman invocation creates {{/var/home/core/.local/share/containers/storage/overlay\-containers/}} with the SELinux context {{data\_home\_t}} instead of the policy\-expected {{container\_ro\_file\_t}}. This context mislabeling causes the test assertion to fail.

The test is tagged {{warn:true}}, so failures produce an UNSTABLE result \(exit code 77\) rather than a hard failure. The test passes consistently on standalone rerun, confirming it is a concurrency/ordering flake, not a true regression.

This has been persistent since build #5214 \(2026\-06\-27\), blocking all non\-x86\_64 rhel\-9.8 builds.

h2. Evidence
h3. Failing Test
{{ext.config.shared.selinux.file\-context\-policy\-match}}

h3. Mislabeled Paths
{{/var/home/core/.local/share/containers/storage/overlay\-containers}} and sub\-paths receive {{data\_home\_t}} instead of {{container\_ro\_file\_t}}

h3. Patterns Observed
* Failure is exclusive to non\-x86\_64 architectures \(s390x, ppc64le, aarch64\)
* Test passes on standalone rerun \({{rerun\_failed: false}}\)
* Repeating since build #5214 \(2026\-06\-27\)
* Test tagged {{warn:true}} → exit code 77 \(UNSTABLE\)
* x86\_64 builds are unaffected \(no concurrent podman race observed\)

h2. Upstream Links
* *Test Source*: [https://github.com/coreos/fedora\-coreos\-config/blob/testing\-devel/tests/kola/selinux/file\-context\-policy\-match|https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-config/blob/testing-devel/tests/kola/selinux/file-context-policy-match]
* *Prior similar issues \(closed\)*: COS\-4147, COS\-4004

h2. Resolution
* *Status*: Unresolved — persistent since 2026\-06\-27

h3. Recommended Fixes \(choose one\)
# *Exception list*: Add {{/var/home/core/.local/share/containers/storage/overlay\-containers}} to the test path exception list in {{coreos/fedora\-coreos\-config}}
# *Exclusive tag*: Mark the test {{exclusive: true}} to prevent concurrent execution with podman\-invoking tests
# *Upstream bug*: File a bug against {{container\-selinux}} to ensure podman creates the directory with the correct {{container\_ro\_file\_t}} label at init time

h2. Root Cause Analysis
* *Classification*: infrastructure \(flake\)
* *Confidence*: high

Build #6678 for stream {{4.21\-9.6}} failed during the x86\_64 {{node\-image\-extensions}} container build step. The {{podman build}} command crashed with exit code 125 while executing {{COPY \-\-from=os /usr/share/rpm\-ostree/extensions/}} — podman reported {{unable to read layer "117f6916...": layer not known}} and {{identifier is not a container}} when trying to commit the build container.

This is a well\-documented transient podman/buildah containers\-storage race condition \(upstream buildah#5674, podman#24598\) that occurs under parallel builds sharing the same storage backend. All other architectures \(s390x, ppc64le, aarch64\) completed successfully with the same Dockerfile and the same openshift/os commit \({{10f1a2e}}\). The identical stream built successfully in prior run #6675.

h2. Evidence
h3. Log Excerpt
{code}
COPY --from=os /usr/share/rpm-ostree/extensions/
unable to read layer "117f6916...": layer not known
identifier is not a container
Error: building at STEP ...: exit status 125
{code}

h3. Patterns Observed
* Failure isolated to x86\_64 extensions container build step only
* All other arches \(s390x, ppc64le, aarch64\) succeeded with same Dockerfile and same openshift/os commit \(10f1a2e\)
* Same stream succeeded in prior run #6675
* podman exit code 125 with "layer not known" / "identifier is not a container" — classic containers\-storage race symptom

h2. Upstream Links
* *Related Issues*: [https://github.com/containers/buildah/issues/5674|https://github.com/containers/buildah/issues/5674], [https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/24598|https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/24598]

h2. Resolution
* *Status*: retry\-pending — transient flake; rerun should succeed
* If recurs frequently on x86\_64, investigate Jenkins builder node's podman/storage health
* Track upstream podman#24598 for permanent fix

* Race condition between podman's internal container registry and cleanup routine
* Affects x86_64 only; other arches unaffected in the same run

h2. Root Cause Analysis
* *Classification*: infrastructure / flake \(recurring\)
* *Confidence*: High

The multi\-stage Dockerfile build completed successfully \(all 3 stages committed and tagged\). The failure occurred in podman's internal post\-build cleanup phase when attempting to delete the intermediate build container after a successful COMMIT. This is a transient race condition between podman and buildah's container lifecycle management. Only x86\_64 was affected — s390x, aarch64, and ppc64le all succeeded in the same run.

This is a *recurring flake* for this stream: previously tracked in COS\-4574 \(build #6540, 2026\-06\-29\) and COS\-4563 \(build #6519, 2026\-06\-28\).

* *Component*: coreos\-assembler / podman
* *Versions*: podman\-5.8.2\-1.fc43.x86\_64, buildah\-1.43.1\-1.fc43.x86\_64 \(inside cosa container, commit e884af8d\)
* *Failing script*: cmd\-remote\-build\-container line 57 — treats any non\-zero podman build exit as fatal, even when the image was already committed

h2. Evidence
h3. Log Excerpt
{code}
[3/3] COMMIT registry.ci.openshift.org/coreos/node-staging:4.20-9.6-node-image-x86_64
Successfully tagged registry.ci.openshift.org/coreos/node-staging:4.20-9.6-node-image-x86_64
time="2026-07-01T10:26:36Z" level=error msg="error deleting build container \"eb8fc0fef104...\": identifier is not a container"

subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '[podman, build, ...]' returned non-zero exit status 125.
{code}

h3. Patterns Observed
* Image build and COMMIT succeed; failure is strictly in post\-COMMIT container cleanup
* podman exits with code 125 after successful tag/push
* Only x86\_64 affected; all other architectures \(s390x, aarch64, ppc64le\) succeed in the same run
* Recurring pattern: 3 failures in 3 days \(2026\-06\-28, 2026\-06\-29, 2026\-07\-01\)

* *Jenkins URL*: [https://jenkins\-rhcos\-\-prod\-pipeline.apps.int.prod\-stable\-spoke1\-dc\-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build\-node\-image/6564/|https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-node-image/6564/]

h2. Root Cause Analysis
* *Classification*: infrastructure \(transient\)
* *Confidence*: high

All four architectures \(x86\_64, aarch64, ppc64le, s390x\) built successfully. Only the ppc64le podman push to registry.ci.openshift.org failed, returning HTTP 400 Bad request during a chunked blob upload. The job exhausted all 5 retries \(\~4m40s total retry time\) without success. The same stream and git ref \(d75a447\) completed successfully 13 hours earlier in build #6545, confirming this is a transient registry\-side issue rather than a code or image problem.

h2. Evidence
h3. Log Excerpt
{code}
15:19:25 Error: writing blob: uploading layer chunked: StatusCode: 400, Bad request
{code}

h3. Patterns Observed
* All 5 podman push retries failed with the same HTTP 400 error
* Only the ppc64le architecture push was affected; x86\_64, aarch64, and s390x succeeded
* Identical stream \+ git ref \(d75a447\) succeeded in build #6545 \~13 hours prior
* HTTP 400 on chunked blob upload is consistent with a load\-balancer or proxy\-side issue at registry.ci.openshift.org

h2. Upstream Links
* *Previous successful build*: build\-node\-image #6545 \(same stream 4.23\-10.2, same git ref d75a447\)

h2. Resolution
* *Status*: retry\-pending
* *Recommended action*: Retry the build. If retries also fail, investigate registry.ci.openshift.org health \(load\-balancer/proxy issues upstream of the registry\).

 - [x] Ensure your local copy is up to date with the upstream main branch (`git@github.com:coreos/butane.git`)
 - [x] Ensure your working directory is clean (`git clean -fdx`)
 - [x] Ensure you can sign commits and any yubikeys/smartcards are plugged in
 - [x] Run `./tag_release.sh <vX.Y.z> <git commit hash>`
 - [x] Push that tag to GitHub

 - [x] Update the spec file in [Fedora](https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/butane):

   - Switch the `Release` back to `1%{?dist}`
   - Remove any patches obsoleted by the new release

 - [x] Download the artifacts and signatures
 - [x] Verify the signatures
 - [x] Find the new tag in the [GitHub tag list](https://github.com/coreos/butane/tags) and click the triple dots menu, and create a draft release for it.

 - [ ] Run `kinit your_account@IPA.REDHAT.COM`
 - [ ] Run `rhpkg new-sources $(spectool -S butane.spec | sed 's:.*/::')`
 - [ ] PR the changes
 - [ ] Get the PR reviewed and merge it
 - [ ] Update your local repo and run `rhpkg build`
 - [ ] File ticket similar to [this one](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ART-3711) to sync the new version to mirror.openshift.com
 - [ ] Wait until mirror.openshift.com is updated and confirm the new version is correct

CentOS Stream 10 packaging:
  - [ ] Create a `rebase-c10s-butane` issue in the internal team-operations repo and follow the steps there

h2. Build Details

* Job: build-node-image
* Build: #6559
* Stream: 4.23-9.8
* Architecture: s390x (failure during s390x upload phase)
* Jenkins URL: [https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-node-image/6559/|https://jenkins-rhcos--prod-pipeline.apps.int.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/build-node-image/6559/]
* Last Good Build: #6544 (SUCCESS, same stream, same git commit d75a447)

h2. Root Cause Analysis

* Classification: infrastructure
* Confidence: high

Build #6559 for stream {{4.23-9.8}} failed during the Brew koji-upload phase for s390x architecture. The {{kinit}} Kerberos authentication call returned a "Generic error" when attempting to authenticate with the brew keytab. This is a transient IPA/KDC infrastructure failure — the same credentials worked successfully for aarch64 (12:50:43) and x86_64 (12:51:08) uploads ~60–75 seconds earlier, but failed at the s390x attempt (12:52:05).

*Important:* All image builds and kola tests completed successfully for all 4 architectures. However, the partial upload left an inconsistent state:

* ✅ aarch64 uploaded: {{rhcos-aarch64-4.23.9.8.202606301235-0}} tagged into {{rhaos-4.23-rhel-9-candidate}}
* ✅ x86_64 uploaded: {{rhcos-x86_64-4.23.9.8.202606301235-0}} tagged into {{rhaos-4.23-rhel-9-candidate}}
* ❌ s390x: not uploaded
* ❌ ppc64le: not uploaded

h2. Evidence

h3. Log Excerpt

{noformat}[Console line 8112] kinit: Generic error (see e-text) while getting initial credentials{noformat}

h3. Patterns Observed

* Kerberos kinit succeeded for aarch64 at 12:50:43 and x86_64 at 12:51:08
* Kerberos kinit failed for s390x at 12:52:05 with "Generic error" — same keytab, ~60s later
* Transient KDC/IPA unavailability window affecting only the s390x upload slot
* Partial Brew upload state: 2 of 4 architectures uploaded, 2 missing (s390x, ppc64le)

h2. Resolution

* Status: unresolved / retry-pending
* Recommended Action: Retry the build; verify or clean up partial Brew uploads ({{rhcos-aarch64-4.23.9.8.202606301235-0}}, {{rhcos-x86_64-4.23.9.8.202606301235-0}}) before retrying to avoid tag conflicts

h2. Routing

* Primary Team: Infrastructure (transient KDC/IPA issue)
* Secondary: CoreOS pipeline team to confirm retry and handle partial Brew upload cleanup

items.toString:
h2. Root Cause

The newly-added kola test {{ext.config.shared.pqc}} (created 2026-06-11, grace period expires *2026-07-11*) fails consistently across all streams and architectures. The test checks that TLS connections to public websites ({{cloud.google.com}}, {{aws.amazon.com}}, {{start.fedoraproject.org}}) negotiate MLKEM (post-quantum key exchange). Instead, connections use {{TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384}} — classical TLS 1.3 without PQC key exchange.

The grace period mechanism currently converts FAIL → WARN → {{exit 77}} → Jenkins UNSTABLE. *After 2026-07-11, these become hard FAILUREs.*

* *Classification:* test_regression (new test with unmet external dependency assumption)
* *Confidence:* High

h2. Affected Builds

|| Build || Job || Stream || Arch || Status || Timestamp ||
| #5066 | build | rhel-9.8 | x86_64 | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-30 |
| #5243 | build-arch | rhel-9.8 | s390x | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-30 |
| #5242 | build-arch | rhel-9.8 | ppc64le | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-30 |
| #5241 | build-arch | rhel-9.8 | aarch64 | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-30 |
| #5044 | build | c9s | x86_64 | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-27 |
| #5222 | build-arch | c9s | s390x | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-27 |
| #5221 | build-arch | c9s | ppc64le | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-27 |
| #5220 | build-arch | c9s | aarch64 | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-27 |
| #5041 | build | rhel-9.8 | x86_64 | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-27 |
| #5216 | build-arch | rhel-9.8 | s390x | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-27 |
| #5215 | build-arch | rhel-9.8 | ppc64le | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-27 |
| #5214 | build-arch | rhel-9.8 | aarch64 | UNSTABLE | 2026-06-27 |

*Streams affected:* rhel-9.8, c9s
*Arches affected:* x86_64, aarch64, ppc64le, s390x (all)

h2. Evidence

h3. Key Log Excerpt

{code}
⏳ Kola test "ext.config.shared.pqc" is in grace period (created: 2026-06-11, expires: 2026-07-11), failures will be warnings.
PQC key exchange not negotiated for https://cloud.google.com: * SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
--- WARN: ext.config.shared.pqc (27.68s)
Setting overall build result to UNSTABLE
{code}

h3. Patterns Observed

* Failure is 100% consistent across all streams (rhel-9.8, c9s) and all arches (x86_64, aarch64, ppc64le, s390x)
* The test depends on external servers (cloud.google.com, aws.amazon.com, start.fedoraproject.org) advertising MLKEM support, which they currently do not
* Grace period masks FAILUREs as UNSTABLE — converts to hard FAIL on *2026-07-11*

h2. Recommended Resolution

# *Investigate* whether OpenSSL / crypto-policies in rhel-9.8 and c9s images actually enables MLKEM by default (client side)
# *Fix the test* to verify client-side MLKEM capability rather than relying on external server negotiation, OR use a controlled/internal test endpoint confirmed to support MLKEM
# *If RHEL 9.8 does not support PQC yet*, add the test to {{kola-denylist.yaml}} for rhel-9.8 and c9s streams
# *Resolution required before 2026-07-11* to prevent hard FAILUREs across all streams/arches

h2. Related Issues

* *COS-4367* (closed) — created this test ({{ext.config.shared.pqc}})
* *COS-4368* (open) — PQC-related tracking

h2. Resolution

* *Status:* Unresolved — action required before 2026-07-11 grace period expiry

h2. Root Cause Analysis
* *Classification*: INFRA \(transient\)
* *Confidence*: High

The multi\-stage Dockerfile build completed successfully for all 3 stages; the image was tagged and committed. The failure occurred in podman's post\-build cleanup phase immediately after a successful build. Only x86\_64 was affected — s390x, aarch64, and ppc64le all succeeded in the same build run. Build #6537 \(same stream/commit\) succeeded \~2 hours earlier, and multiple prior builds succeeded on the same day. No code or package change is implicated.

h2. Evidence
h3. Log Excerpt
{code}
error deleting build container ... identifier is not a container
podman build exited with code 125
{code}

h3. Patterns Observed
* All 3 Dockerfile stages completed and image was committed before the error
* Failure is isolated to the podman cleanup phase \(post\-build container teardown\)
* Race condition between podman's internal container registry and cleanup routine
* Affects x86\_64 only; other arches unaffected in the same run
* Identical stream/commit succeeded 2 hours prior in build #6537

h2. Resolution
* *Status*: Retry recommended — transient issue, no code regression
* *Action*: Re\-run build\-node\-image for 4.20\-9.6; no code or config changes required

{{podman push}} of the ppc64le node image to {{registry.ci.openshift.org/coreos/node\-staging:4.20\-9.6\-node\-image\-ppc64le}} failed with HTTP 500 from the registry during blob reuse check.
